docs.title: Welcome to GEOG 3319 Geographic Field Techniques
docs.text: Hi there! Welcome to my GitHub repository, where I share teaching material. I'm excited to have you here!

docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
I am an Assistant Professor (AP) in Geography Department at The University of Central Arkansas.

I hold a Ph.D. from the Department of Geospatial Information Sciences at the University of Texas at Dallas (德州大学达拉斯分校).

docs.title: 1. Install the Visual Studio Code (VS Code)¶
docs.text: Install Visual Studio Code

docs.title: 2. Install Anaconda¶
docs.text: To install Anaconda, download the installer from the Anaconda website. The installer will ask you to accept the license agreement, choose the installation directory.

docs.title: 3. Select interpreter in VS code¶
docs.text:
if it is your first time to select interpretr, you need to install two extensions from extensions in the left side bar:

  • Python
  • Jupyter

docs.title: The Python:Select Interpreter (Ctrl+Shift+P) command displays a list of available gloabl environments, conda environments, and virtual environments.¶
4. Create a Juputer Notebook¶
docs.text:
You can create a Jupyter Notebook by running the Create: New Jupyter Notebook command from the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) or by creating a new .ipynb file in your workspace.

Or, you can select 'File' > 'New File'

docs.text: You can save your Jupyter Notebook using the keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+S) or File > Save.

docs.title: 10.1 Create a virtual environment in terminal¶
docs.text:
Right click the Anaconda prompt and Run as Administrator (This step will ensure that your package is installed in Anaconda/env folder)

The following command creates a conda environment named np with a Python 3.9 interpreter

conda create -n np python=3.9

docs.title: 10.2 Check conda is installed¶
docs.text: conda -V

docs.title: 10.3 List virtual environment¶
docs.text:
now if you list virgual envionment, you can see the virtual environment that you just create.

conda env list

For example, I have three virtual environment: base, arcpu_pro, np

docs.title: 10.4 Activate virtual environment¶
docs.text:
if you virtual environment named as 'np'

activate np

docs.title: 10.5 Install packages (e.g., numpy)¶
docs.text: conda install numpy

docs.title: 11. Delete a no longer needed virtual environment¶
docs.text:
For example, delete a virtual environment 'np'

conda remove -n np --all -y

def preprocess_data(df):
    """
    Preprocesses the input DataFrame containing 311 data.

    Parameters:
        df (DataFrame): Input DataFrame containing 311 service request data.

    Returns:
        DataFrame: Preprocessed DataFrame with separate latitude and longitude columns.
    """
    import pandas as pd

    # Convert 'created_date' column to datetime format
    df['created_date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['created_date'], errors='coerce')

    # Select desired columns
    want_col = ["service_request_number", "service_request_type", "created_date", "lat_location"]
    part_df = df[want_col].copy()

    # Extract latitude and longitude from 'lat_location' column
    # Example format: "(32.83108631962040000,-96.85465316346955000)"
    part_df[['latitude', 'longitude']] = (
        part_df['lat_location']
        .str.replace(r"[()]", "", regex=True)  # remove parentheses
        .str.split(",", expand=True)  # split into two columns
        .astype(float)  # convert strings to numeric
    )

    # Create a formatted date column
    part_df['date'] = part_df['created_date'].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")

    return part_df

processed_df = preprocess_data(df)

# Rename the columns using the column_mapping dictionary
processed_df.rename(columns=column_mapping, inplace=True)

docs.title: Set up ArcGIS Pro Account¶
docs.text:
You should get an invitation email to set up your ArcGIS account

The account is composed by your user name and clarku, e.g., yanawu_clarku.

docs.title: Log in ArcGIS Online¶
docs.text:
• Log in ArcGIS Online

  • At the top of the page, click your username and click My settings.

  • On the My settings page, click the Licenses side tab

  • Next to ArcGIS Pro, click Download ArcGIS Pro (If you don't see ArcGIS Pro listed under your licensed products, please contact HelpDesk and JoDolan@clarku.edu).

  • In the Download ArcGIS Pro window, review the language setting. To download a localized version of ArcGIS Pro, change the setting to the language you want.

  • Click Download.

An executable file (.exe) is downloaded to your computer.
